hints: Differentiate y=e^(−5x)ln(5x) with the product and chain rules.
At the stated stationary point x=p set the derivative to zero, cancel the positive exponential factor, and rearrange to the required equation.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = \mathrm{e}^{-5x}\ln(5x)$ using the product rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(uv) = u'v + uv'$:
$$u = \mathrm{e}^{-5x} \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x} = -5\mathrm{e}^{-5x}$$
$$v = \ln(5x) \implies \dfrac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{1}{5x} \times 5 = \dfrac{1}{x}$$

Set $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$ at the stationary point $x = p$:
$$\mathrm{e}^{-5p}\left(-5\ln(5p) + \dfrac{1}{p}\right) = 0$$
$$\text{Since } \mathrm{e}^{-5p} > 0 \text{ for all real } p, \quad -5\ln(5p) + \dfrac{1}{p} = 0$$
$$5\ln(5p) = \dfrac{1}{p} \implies \ln(5p) = \dfrac{1}{5p}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Stationary Points: Applies the product or quotient rule, e.g. $e^{-5x}\dfrac{d}{dx}(\ln5x)+\ln5x\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^{-5x})$. Derives the derivative, e.g. $\dfrac1x e^{-5x}-5e^{-5x}\ln5x$. The final result is $\ln5p=\dfrac1{5p}$.

hints: Sketch y=ln(5x) for x>0, increasing from −∞ and crossing the axis at x=1/5.
Sketch y=1/(5x), positive and strictly decreasing with both axes as asymptotes; show exactly one intersection.
walkthrough:
Consider the two functions $y = \ln(5x)$ and $y = \dfrac{1}{5x}$ for $x > 0$:
$$\text{The graph of } y = \ln(5x) \text{ is strictly increasing, has a vertical asymptote at } x = 0 \text{ with } y \to -\infty,$$
$$\text{and crosses the } x\text{-axis at } 5x = 1 \implies x = 0.2.$$

Analyze the hyperbola $y = \dfrac{1}{5x}$:
$$\text{For } x > 0, \; y = \dfrac{1}{5x} > 0 \text{ is strictly decreasing, with } y \to \infty \text{ as } x \to 0^+ \text{ and } y \to 0 \text{ as } x \to \infty.$$

Conclude on the number of intersections:
$$\text{Since one curve is strictly increasing from } -\infty \text{ to } +\infty \text{ and the other is strictly decreasing to } 0,$$
$$\text{the graphs of } y = \ln(5x) \text{ and } y = \dfrac{1}{5x} \text{ intersect at exactly one point for } x > 0.$$
$$\text{Therefore, the equation } \ln(5p) = \dfrac{1}{5p} \text{ has only one root.}$$

ai_rubric.Graphical Root Analysis: The graphs $y=\ln5x$ and $y=1/(5x)$ have exactly one intersection for $x>0$.

hints: Evaluate f(0.2) and f(0.6), show opposite signs, and use continuity to prove the strict bracket.
walkthrough: Define the continuous difference function $f(p) = \ln(5p) - \dfrac{1}{5p}$ for $p > 0$:

Conclude using the sign change theorem:
$$\text{Since } f(0.2) < 0 \text{ and } f(0.6) > 0, \text{ and } f(p) \text{ is continuous on } [0.2, 0.6],$$
$$\text{a root } p \text{ lies in the interval } 0.2 < p < 0.6.$$

ai_rubric.Numerical Root Bracketing: Endpoint evaluations at 0.2 and 0.6 establish the sign change or ordering. Endpoint evaluation gives $f(p)=\ln5p-1/(5p)$, $f(0.2)=-1<0$ and $f(0.6)=0.765>0$, so $0.2<p<0.6$.

hints: Record every iterate to 4 decimal places until the alternating values justify a 2-decimal-place result.
walkthrough:
Set up the iterative formula $p_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{5p_n}}$ starting with an initial guess, e.g. $p_1 = 0.4000$:
$$\dfrac{1}{5p_1} = \dfrac{1}{5(0.4)} = \dfrac{1}{2} = 0.5$$
$$p_2 = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{0.5} \approx \dfrac{1.648721}{5} \approx 0.3297$$

Perform successive iterations to 4 decimal places:
$$p_3 = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{5(0.3297)}} = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{0.606612} \approx \dfrac{1.834208}{5} \approx 0.3668$$
$$p_4 = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{5(0.3668)}} = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{0.545256} \approx 0.3450$$
$$p_5 = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{5(0.3450)}} \approx 0.3571$$
$$p_6 = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{5(0.3571)}} \approx 0.3502$$
$$p_7 = \dfrac{1}{5}\mathrm{e}^{\frac{1}{5(0.3502)}} \approx 0.3541$$

Conclude the value of $p$ correct to 2 decimal places:
$$\text{Since successive iterates oscillate tightly around } 0.352, \text{ all values round to:}$$
$$p = 0.35$$

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Substitution into $p=\dfrac15\exp\!\left(\dfrac1{5p}\right)$ produces successive numerical iterates; the stabilized value is $p=0.35$ (2 d.p.); for example from $p_1=0.4$: $0.4000,0.3297,0.3668,0.3450,0.3571,0.3502,0.3541$.
